title: should / shouldn't for Health Advice
grammarNote: SHOULD используется для дачи совета или рекомендации — это мягкое "нужно". SHOULDN'T — совет против чего-то делать. Важно: should — это НЕ обязательство (не must/have to). Это просто рекомендация: "Я думаю, что это хорошая идея для тебя." Структура: subject + should/shouldn't + base form (без to).

grammarTable.subject: You should
grammarTable.example: "You should drink more water." / "She should sleep earlier."

grammarTable.subject: You shouldn't
grammarTable.example: "You shouldn't skip meals." / "He shouldn't work so late."

grammarTable.subject: Should I...?
grammarTable.example: "Should I take vitamins?" / "Should we call a doctor?"

grammarTable.subject: You should have
grammarTable.example: "You should have slept earlier." (but you didn't)

grammarTable.subject: Form
grammarTable.example: "She should eat." (NOT "she shoulds eat" — modals don't change!)

rows.example: "You should get more sleep." / "She should see a doctor." / "He should eat breakfast."
"You shouldn't drink so much coffee." / "You shouldn't study all night."
"Should I take a day off?" / "Should we call an ambulance?" / "What should I do?"
"You should try to exercise more." / "You should try to reduce screen time."

grammarExtra.title: should vs must vs have to

rows.example: "You should sleep more." (recommendation — it's a good idea)
"You have to be at work by 9." (it's required by someone/something)
"You shouldn't eat so much sugar." (advice) vs "You mustn't enter." (forbidden — rule)
You didn't sleep earlier — that was a mistake. Past criticism/regret. ✅
She didn't eat breakfast — that was a bad idea. ✅
I drank too much — and now I regret it. ✅
"should + have + past participle" — only for past. "You should have rested." ✅
✅ "You should drink water." — no "to" after modals! ✅
✅ "Should you drink water?" — this asks for advice. ✅
✅ "You shouldn't skip it." — no "to" after should/shouldn't. ✅

grammarTip:
SHOULD / SHOULDN'T — совет и рекомендация:

should + base form (без TO!):
"You should drink more water." ✅
"You should get some rest." ✅

shouldn't + base form:
"You shouldn't skip meals." ✅
"She shouldn't work so late." ✅

⚠️ Типичные ошибки:
✗ "She shoulds sleep." → ✅ "She should sleep."
✗ "You should to rest." → ✅ "You should rest."

Прошедшее время (критика/сожаление):
"You should have slept earlier." (но ты не спал)
"I shouldn't have eaten so much." (но я съел)

Сила совета:
should (рекомендация) < must/have to (обязательство)

exercises.text: You ___ drink more water — you're dehydrated.
exercises.hint: "should" + base form (NO "to"). "You SHOULD DRINK more water." ✅

exercises.text: She ___ stay up so late — she has an exam tomorrow.
exercises.hint: "shouldn't" + base form. "She SHOULDN'T STAY up so late." ✅

exercises.text: "You ___ skip breakfast. It's the most important meal of the day."

exercises.instruction: Form a question asking for advice.
exercises.text: "___ I see a doctor about this headache?"
exercises.hint: "Should I...?" = asking for advice. "SHOULD I see a doctor?" ✅
✅ "She SHOULD exercise more." — modals NEVER take -s. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose: should, must, or have to?
exercises.text: "You ___ eat more vegetables." (strong advice from a doctor)
exercises.hint: A doctor's advice = "should". "You SHOULD eat more vegetables." ✅

exercises.instruction: Complete with should have + past participle.
exercises.text: "You ___ (sleep) earlier last night. You look exhausted."
exercises.hint: Past criticism: "You SHOULD HAVE SLEPT earlier." = you didn't, and that was a mistake. ✅

exercises.text: "You shouldn't drink so much coffee." means:
opts: I advise you not to — it's not a good idea
exercises.correct: I advise you not to — it's not a good idea
exercises.hint: "shouldn't" = advice against doing something. ✅ Not forbidden, not impossible.

opts: "Should you eat less sugar." (as a statement)
exercises.hint: "should" + base form (no "to", no "-s"). "You SHOULD eat less sugar." ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (eat) so much last night. I feel terrible."
exercises.hint: Past regret: "I SHOULDN'T HAVE EATEN so much." = I ate too much and regret it. ✅

exercises.text: "What should I do about my headaches?" — Good advice:
opts: "You should to rest and drink water."
exercises.hint: "should" + base form. "You SHOULD REST and DRINK water." ✅

exercises.text: "You ___ enter the laboratory without protective equipment." (rule / safety law)
exercises.hint: "mustn't" = forbidden by rule. "MUSTN'T enter without protection." ✅ vs "shouldn't" = advice only.

questions.hint: "should" = advice; recommendation. Not as strong as "must." ✅

opts: "Shoulds" is never correct — modals don't change
questions.correct: "Shoulds" is never correct — modals don't change
questions.hint: Modal verbs NEVER add -s. "She SHOULD exercise." ✅ Never "shoulds."

questions.text: "You should to drink water." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: "should" + BASE FORM (no "to"). "You should DRINK water." ✅ Never "should to drink."

questions.text: "___ I take a day off?" — Asking for advice:
"You should have slept earlier." — This means:
opts: You slept early and that was good
You didn't sleep early — that was a mistake
questions.correct: You didn't sleep early — that was a mistake
questions.hint: "should have + pp" = past criticism. You didn't do it, but you should have. ✅

questions.text: "I ___ (eat) so much cake. I feel terrible." (past regret)
questions.hint: "shouldn't have eaten" = I ate too much and now regret it. Past form. ✅

questions.text: "You shouldn't drink coffee late." vs "You must not enter." — Difference:
questions.hint: "shouldn't" = not a good idea (advice). "Must not" = forbidden/prohibited. ✅

questions.text: "You should try to exercise." — "Should" here is:
questions.hint: "should" = recommendation. "You SHOULD try to exercise." = I advise you to. ✅

questions.text: "What ___ I do about this headache?" (asking for advice)
questions.hint: "What SHOULD I do?" = asking for a recommendation. ✅

questions.text: "You should have seen a doctor." — Form: should + have + ___.

questions.hint: "should" = advice. "must" = obligation. "should" is WEAKER — a suggestion, not a command. ✅

questions.text: You give advice to a friend who is stressed. Which is most appropriate?
questions.hint: "should" is most appropriate for friendly advice. "Must" and "have to" sound too strong. ✅

questions.text: "You shouldn't have stayed up so late." means:
opts: Don't stay up late in the future
You stayed up late — that was a mistake
You are not allowed to stay up late
You don't need to stay up late
questions.correct: You stayed up late — that was a mistake
questions.hint: "shouldn't have + pp" = past criticism. You did it, but you shouldn't have. ✅
